subject: Aurora – provisioning & burst guardrails for Q4 launch
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orenda.health>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora – provisioning & burst guardrails for Q4 launch

Marcus — thanks again for the call this morning. A couple of clarifying points from our side so we can align capacity and procurement: 1) Our launch day traffic model shows a sustained ramp over 90 minutes to ~45 RPM (concurrent interactive sessions) with average generation of ~150 tokens per response; 2) We have a hard p95 latency requirement of <= 600ms for the patient-facing flows and a softer internal SLO of <= 350ms for clinicians; 3) Procurement asked for a conservative baseline commit number so they can budget.

Can you send the quick back-of-the-envelope GPU count with options for: conservative commit (lowest cost), recommended commit (runway + headroom), and a burst/market policy for short spikes? We need this by Friday to prep the internal ask.

— Sanjay

On Thu, May 21, 2026 at 08:03 Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sanjay — capturing notes and will sketch three options.
> — Marcus
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orenda.health>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora capacity sketch — numbers & assumptions (v1)

Sanjay — attaching the workbook (aurora_capacity_calc_v3.xlsx). High-level assumptions used: model = redwood/13B-chat-q4-q4f (quantized 4-bit), avg response length = 150 tokens, steady RPM = 45 (equates to 45 req/s sustained), peak multiple = 3x launch spike, planned KV/prefix cache applicability = 20% of tokens, batching = avg batch size 12 during steady load, 16 during peak.

Quick numbers (rounded):
- Baseline load: 45 req/s * 150 tokens = 6,750 tokens/sec.
- Peak (3x): 20,250 tokens/sec.
- Effective tokens after cache (20% reduction): baseline ~5,400 t/s, peak ~16,200 t/s.
- Measured per-GPU effective throughput (13B-q4 w/our runtime, p95 latency ~350ms at target batch): ~420 tokens/sec per GPU.

Raw GPU math:
- Conservative (cost-first, commit): plan for baseline with minimal cushion: ceil(5,400 / 420) = 13 GPUs.
- Recommended (runway + 50% headroom): target capacity = 16,200 * 1.5 = 24,300 -> ceil(24,300 / 420) = 58 GPUs.
- Hybrid (commit + burst): commit 32 GPUs (covers steady + some growth, ~13k t/s) + autoscale/market burst to 72 GPUs for launch windows (gives ~30k t/s capacity).

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- If Orenda can increase prefix caching to 35% (more static prompts), effective tokens drop further and recommended GPUs fall ~20% (roughly 46 GPUs in recommended case).
- Quantization to q4 is assumed — if they require fp16 for quality, per-GPU throughput drops ~40% (and GPU counts increase accordingly).
- Burst policy: we recommend two-tier bursts: (a) short warm-up burst to +25% for 3–10 minutes using pre-warmed machines (no model swap), (b) market burst with capacity up to +100% for up to 60 minutes; include fallback to a smaller model variant with lower latency if market burst fails.

I put the detailed sensitivity tabs in the workbook. If these look sane, we can translate to committed SKU counts and draft the procurement ask.

— Marcus

Attachment: aurora_capacity_calc_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora capacity sketch — numbers & assumptions (v1)

Looping in ops notes — quick operational sanity checks and an alternative batch/caching config we should offer Orenda: 

Operational sanity checklist:
- Warm pool: pre-warm 8 machines in the slab to avoid cold-start latency for the first 20 minutes of launch traffic.
- KV caching: ensure Orenda's session design sets patient prompts as prefix cacheable for at least 120s to capture repeat flows.
- Canary: canary 10% traffic on the new slab for 48 hours post-launch, with automatic switchover if p95 > 900ms for 5 consecutive minutes.

Alternative configuration to reduce committed GPUs:
- Increase batching aggressiveness during steady windows (batch target 14) and rely on smarter batching windows for patient flows where 600ms is acceptable. This pushes per-GPU throughput from 420 -> ~500 t/s but increases tail risk.
- With that configuration and 20% cache, recommended capacity becomes ceil(24,300 / 500) = 49 GPUs (vs 58).

Trade-off summary (short):
- 13 GPUs: minimal commit, risk on growth and spikes — cheaper but no runway.
- 32 commit + burst to 72: balanced — gives procurement a clear commit and ops a burst runway.
- 49–58 GPUs recommended depending on batching/caching tradeoffs and quality constraints.

Priyom
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orenda.health>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, procurement@orenda.health
Date: 2026-05-24T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora – provisioning & burst guardrails for Q4 launch (procurement ask)

Sanjay / procurement team — thanks for the patience. Based on the numbers Marcus and Priyom shared, here is a procurement-friendly proposal you can take to your finance: 

Proposal (recommended):
- Committed slab: 32 GPUs (redwood-dedicated-p4x16, quantized 13B profile) for a 12-month initial term. This covers steady-state and short growth windows.
- Burst buffer: automatic market burst up to 72 GPUs for launch-day windows and marketing spikes (30 days of aggregated burst minutes priced at pay-as-you-go).
- Headroom / safety: pre-warm 8 machines in the slab, canary 10% for 48 hours.
- SLA: p95 latency target <= 600ms for patient flows, with credits for >3 consecutive 5-minute windows breaching that threshold. Draft SLA attached.

Rationale: 32 commit hits a middle ground for procurement — keeps monthly committed cost predictable while giving ops the ability to scale to the recommended runway size for major events. If Orenda is willing to accept more aggressive batching or increase prefix cacheable content, we can reduce the committed slab (we noted 49 GPUs as an optimized commit in that scenario).

Next steps: 
1) Sanjay / procurement — confirm whether you prefer the 32-commit + burst model or a larger fixed commit (we can price both).
2) If you want the lower-cost commit, we will provide a short runbook for cache/batching changes to protect latency.

Attachment: SLA_draft_orenda.docx (30KB)

— Kimberly
